body: ## Propane at number one

Bottled or tank gas heats 210 of Berlin's 1,432 occupied homes. According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022), that is 14.7%, the highest share of all 50 towns Mass HVAC serves, against 4.5% for the middle town. Fuel oil or kerosene still leads at 646 homes (45.1%), ranked 19th, and utility gas follows with 392 (27.4%), ranked 33rd. Electricity heats 149 homes (10.4%), 24th.

Fuel that arrives by truck and sits in a tank heats most of the town, so a replacement decision often includes the tank and the delivery arrangement as well as the boiler or furnace. A heat pump, which runs on electricity, changes that picture for the part of the load it carries.
## The newest housing stock in the area

Berlin's median home was built in 1995, which makes it the newest median of the 50 towns (the middle town's is 1975). Units from 2000 or later number 688, or 46.0% of the total, and 282 (18.8%) were built since 2010, the 2nd-highest share. Only 587 units (39.2%) predate 1980, ranking 48th, while the middle town sits at 57.2%.

The old and the new sit side by side. The sheet also counts 290 units from 1939 or earlier (19.4%), the 16th-highest share, plus 110 from 1940 to 1959, 187 from 1960 to 1979 and 222 from 1980 to 1999. A house from one band can need a very different size of equipment than one from another, which is why we assess the home's heating load before quoting a system.
## Houses, townhouses and small buildings

Berlin's 1,497 housing units are 56.1% single-family detached houses (840), a rank of 43rd, well below the 76.7% of the middle town. Attached townhouses are 371 units (24.8%). Duplex-style buildings hold 127 units (8.5%), small buildings of three or four units hold 17, and larger ones of five or more hold 142 (9.5%). All multi-unit buildings together hold 286 units (19.1%), 20th of 50. With 265 renter households (18.5%), the town sits above the 16.4% renter share of the middle town.
## National Grid and the rebate path

Berlin appears on National Grid's official Massachusetts Electric Company territory list. The Mass Save program is therefore the place to start when you price a heat pump, and the [heat pump page](/cities/berlin/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) explains how Berlin's housing meets the weatherization condition.
## Hills, rivers and farm stock

Berlin lies in a low range of hills between the Nashua River and Assabet River valleys, 12 miles northeast of Worcester and 29 miles west of Boston. It covers 13.1 square miles, of which 12.9 are land and 0.2 are water (1.22%). It borders Hudson and Marlborough to the east, Bolton to the north, Clinton and Boylston to the west and Northborough to the south. Interstate 495 and Route 62 run through town, and Berlin is the center of population for New England.

The land was first settled in 1665, and the town was incorporated in 1812. Residents farmed hay, grains and cattle, and after the Civil War a large shoe factory and lumbering gave non-farm jobs. The town then turned to specialty market gardening, sending 41,000 bunches of asparagus to market in 1885, and by 1940 its poultry farmers produced 836,600 dozen eggs a year.

The first town house went up in 1831, and a new town hall was built from 1869 to 1870. The town hall moved to the former elementary school building in 1998, and the 1870 hall was refurbished with accessible access to its second floor in 2019.

body: ## The oil and gas side of the mix

Beyond bottled gas, the 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) shows Berlin split between oil and utility gas. Oil heats 646 homes (45.1%). Utility gas heats 392 (27.4%), ranked 33rd of 50. Electricity heats 149 (10.4%), and the survey records 9 homes with solar, 8 with wood and 18 with other fuels.
Oil leads, yet no single fuel covers a majority, so a failed boiler or furnace may lead anywhere. A household can stay with the same fuel, move to a gas main if one is near, or look at a heat pump.
### Permits for gas equipment
New gas furnaces and boilers normally come with a permit and a final inspection. The permit itself has to come from a licensed plumber or gas fitter. The building department can explain local steps.
### Rental heat

Berlin has 265 renter households (18.5%). For those tenants the state sanitary code sets a minimum of 68 F by day and 64 F overnight during the heating season, and heat is the landlord's cost unless the lease says otherwise (general information, not legal advice). A rental boiler is most likely to give out in a cold snap, which is the moment tenants notice.
### An old core in a new town

Most Berlin housing is new, but 290 units were built in 1939 or earlier (19.4%, 16th of 50). Those oldest houses can have heat loss and layouts unlike the 688 units from 2000 or later. A boiler matched to a neighbor's house may not suit them, so we assess the home's heating load before quoting.
### Heat that stops

Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. We are licensed and insured, take urgent calls around the clock, and put a free written estimate in your hands before any work begins. Our [maintenance page](/cities/berlin/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers keeping the system running afterward.

faq.q: Is gas a realistic option for a Berlin home on oil?
faq.a: If a main reaches the street, yes. Utility gas already heats 27.4% of occupied homes, so lines exist in part of town. The gas company decides if your street qualifies. If not, the choices are oil, propane, which is common in Berlin, or a heat pump.

faq.q: How does a rental landlord handle a heat failure?
faq.a: Heat is normally the landlord's expense unless the lease assigns it elsewhere, and a state code sets minimum temperatures for the heating season. A tenant should report the outage right away. Berlin counts 265 renting households, so the question is a real one (general information, not legal advice).

faq.q: Do newer Berlin homes need different heating equipment?
faq.a: Often a smaller capacity, because newer houses tend to be tighter and better insulated. That is general, not guaranteed. With 46.0% of units built in 2000 or later, many houses fit this description, but a heating load assessment is the way to confirm the size for any particular house.

body: ## A town with more variety than most

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 840 detached houses among Berlin's 1,497 units. What remains is varied: 371 townhouse units, 127 units in two-unit buildings, 17 in three- and four-unit buildings, and 142 in the largest buildings. Add them all up and multi-unit buildings hold 286 units, 19.1%, which ranks 20th.
Median owner-occupied value is $570,300, 26th of 50 and close to the middle town's $579,150.
### Cooling an attached home

A townhouse or small multi-unit home has fewer exterior walls, so the outdoor unit may end up on a pad, a balcony or a common area, and whoever manages the property may have a say. Berlin's 24.8% townhouse share makes that a regular question rather than an exception. Ductless mini-splits can serve one unit without running ducts through shared walls, which makes them a natural fit for attached housing.
### Cooling a detached house

With 840 detached units, central air and ductless both remain on the table. Central air depends on ducts that are sound and big enough for cooling air, and a duct run built only for heating is often undersized. A ductless head can cover a room that central air reaches poorly.
### Newer homes, smaller loads

In the 2000-or-later group of 688 units, tighter walls and newer windows usually mean a lighter cooling load, so a modest system may be enough. Oversizing is the trap: an oversized unit satisfies the thermostat quickly and quits before drying the air, which can leave the rooms clammy. The load, not the old nameplate, should set the size.
### Repairs and replacement

Small faults such as a weak capacitor or a fouled coil are normally repairs. When the compressor itself has died on an aging unit, replacement is the likelier outcome. Either way the estimate is written and free, and it arrives before work starts. If you are weighing a system that heats and cools, see the [heat pump page](/cities/berlin/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Can I put an air conditioner in a Berlin townhouse?
faq.a: Usually, but placement needs thought. Berlin has 371 attached townhouse units, and shared walls limit where outdoor equipment can go. With ductless there is no ductwork to route, though a landlord or association may need to approve where the outdoor unit goes. Ask about rules before ordering anything.

faq.q: Is ductless better than central air for an older house?
faq.a: Often, if the house has no ducts. Ductless heads cool room by room and need only a small opening for the line set. Berlin has 290 units built in 1939 or earlier. Central air is the better match where the ductwork is already sound.

faq.q: How long should an air conditioner last before replacement?
faq.a: There is no fixed number, since it depends on the equipment, installation and use. Signs that replacement is near include repeated repairs, a failed compressor, refrigerant leaks and rising bills. A written estimate that lays out repair and replacement costs side by side makes the choice easier.

For 2026, Mass Save pays $2,650 per ton toward a whole-home heat pump, capped at $8,500, if the house is weatherized enough first. The rest of the rules live on the [statewide heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

Build year alone clears the weatherization condition for 2000 and later. In Berlin that covers 688 units (46.0%), including 282 built since 2010. At the other end, 587 units (39.2%) predate 1980, ranking 48th, so the assessment route applies to a smaller group than in most towns.
### National Grid territory
National Grid appears on the official territory list for Berlin, so Mass Save is the first program to check. Because terms change, read the current ones at masssave.com.
### Propane and oil households

Bottled gas heats 210 Berlin homes (14.7%, first among the 50 towns), and oil heats 646. Both come by truck, so each part of the load a heat pump takes over is fuel that need not be delivered. Electricity heats 149 homes today, and utility gas serves 392. The 149 electric homes show that electric heat is already part of the mix. For the 392 gas homes, the comparison is between two fuels that both have a monthly bill.
### Propane and the sizing question

Because propane equipment is common here, the first step for those owners is a heating load assessment before quoting. The result shows what capacity a heat pump needs and whether a partial setup, with the old system left in place for the coldest days, makes sense.
### Townhouses and shared walls

Berlin has 371 townhouse units and 286 units in multi-unit buildings. A ductless system can serve a single unit, and the outdoor unit placement may need approval from an association or landlord. With 24.8% of housing in townhouses, that is a common point to settle early.
### Ducted or ductless

A ducted heat pump reuses good ductwork. Ductless heads suit additions, older rooms and units without ducts. See our [cooling page](/cities/berlin/air-conditioning-installation-repair) for how ductless fits attached homes.

faq.q: Does a house built after 2000 automatically qualify?
faq.a: It meets the weatherization condition by build year, which is one of the program's requirements. Others still apply, such as the equipment installation window in 2026 and an eligible installer. That is 688 Berlin units, a large share of the housing. Confirm all terms at masssave.com.

faq.q: I have propane in Berlin. Is a heat pump worth considering?
faq.a: It is worth pricing. Berlin has the highest share of bottled-gas homes of the 50 towns, 14.7%, and a heat pump can take over part or all of the heating that would otherwise be delivered. A heating load assessment gives the size, and a partial setup can keep the propane system for the coldest days.

faq.q: Which rebate applies if I am in National Grid territory?
faq.a: Mass Save is the program to start with, and the whole-home and partial-home rebates are described on our statewide heat pump page. Eligibility depends on the home, the installer and the dates, and terms can change, so confirm everything at masssave.com before you commit.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Berlin burns oil in 646 homes, propane or bottled gas in 210 and utility gas in 392, so most systems have a flame to keep clean. With 18.5% of households renting, tune-ups also depend on who books them.
body: ## Three kinds of flame, three checklists

The oil burner needs a cleaning once a year, before the heating season: soot removed, filter and nozzle replaced, combustion checked. Oil heats 646 Berlin homes. Bottled or tank gas heats 210, the highest share of any of the 50 towns, and utility gas heats 392. Gas burners get a safety check of the burner, flue and controls.
### Owners and landlords

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022) counts 1,167 owner-occupied households (81.5%) and 265 renters (18.5%, 22nd of 50). An owner books the visit personally. A landlord who pays for heat has a reason to schedule a check before the first cold week.
### Age of the housing

Berlin has 688 units from 2000 or later and 222 from 1980 to 1999 (14.8%). Newer equipment tends to need fewer repairs, but filters, condensate drains and combustion settings still drift out of adjustment, and a spring or fall visit resets them. The 187 units from 1960 to 1979 (12.5%) and the 110 from 1940 to 1959 (7.3%) may have older equipment, which is where a planned visit finds worn parts early.
### Vacant and seasonal

Berlin has 65 vacant units (4.3%), ranking 20th and above the 3.6% of the middle town. A house left empty through a winter stretch needs its heat kept at a safe minimum, and it should have a system check before the owner returns. An unnoticed fault in an empty building can run for weeks, and frozen pipes are the usual result.
### A yearly rhythm
- **Late summer to early fall:** heating tune-up.
- **Spring:** cooling check on central air or ductless heads.
- **Whenever it happens:** a burner that starts and stops, an odd smell or a climbing bill deserves a call.
If a visit finds a failed unit, see our [heating page](/cities/berlin/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should a propane or oil system be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year is the usual practice, ahead of the heating season. An oil burner is cleaned and gets a new filter and nozzle. Gas appliances get their burner, flue and controls checked. Berlin has both in numbers, with 646 oil homes and 210 on bottled gas.

It is a sensible step. Heat is normally the landlord's cost unless the lease shifts it, and rental equipment tends to give out when the temperature drops. Berlin has 265 renter households, and a pre-season service lowers the chance of an emergency call at the worst time.

faq.q: Does a newer system still need a tune-up?
faq.a: Yes, age alone does not exempt it. Filters, drains, burners and electrical connections need regular attention whatever the age. Almost half of Berlin units are from 2000 or later (46.0%), and systems in those houses still benefit from a yearly check, plus a quick look before the cooling season. Small faults caught early are cheaper than faults that run for a season.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Berlin pairs 688 units built in 2000 or later with 290 from 1939 or earlier. Tight newer houses can trap moisture and fumes, older ones leak, and the right fix depends on measurements in the house itself.
body: ## Tight new houses and leaky old ones

According to the 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022), Berlin's housing divides into 290 units from 1939 or earlier (19.4%), 110 from 1940 to 1959 (7.3%), 187 from 1960 to 1979 (12.5%), 222 from 1980 to 1999 (14.8%) and 688 from 2000 or later (46.0%). That puts close to half the housing in the era of tighter construction.
### Newer, tighter houses

A tight house saves energy and also keeps damp air, cooking fumes and chemicals from furnishings indoors unless ventilation works. A ventilator that moves stale air out and fresh air in is the usual answer. The 282 units built since 2010 (18.8%) are the most likely to fit that description.
### Older houses

Houses from 1939 or earlier, 290 here, often leak air through gaps. Those gaps thin out some indoor pollutants, yet they also carry in dust, pollen and damp air. Before renovating one, ask a specialist about testing for older materials. Berlin's 290 oldest units are 19.4% of the housing, a larger share than the 16.6% of the middle town.
### Fuel and combustion

Propane heats 210 Berlin homes, oil 646 and utility gas 392. A flame appliance needs a clear vent and a clean burner, because combustion byproducts count as an indoor air problem. Carbon monoxide detectors are worth having in any home that burns fuel.
### Humidity
Dry air in winter and damp air in summer are common. Measuring humidity with a hygrometer shows which one applies, and a humidifier, dehumidifier or ventilator then answers a real reading.
### Ducts, filters and testing

Filters catch what passes through the system, so keeping one clean helps. Duct cleaning makes sense for visible dirt, mold or damage. One air test captures a single day, so what lasts is a repair at the source: a leaky duct, an unvented appliance or a wet basement. Equipment care helps too; see the [maintenance page](/cities/berlin/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do new Berlin houses need ventilation?
faq.a: Often. The tighter a house is, the less natural air exchange it has, so moisture, fumes and chemicals can build up. About 46.0% of Berlin units date from 2000 or later. A ventilator or a properly set exhaust fan supplies fresh air. Measuring humidity first shows how much help the house needs.

faq.q: Is old housing always worse for air quality?
faq.a: No. A leaky house dilutes some pollutants, though it also admits dust and damp air. Berlin has 290 units from 1939 or earlier, and their condition varies widely. Testing and inspection tell you more than age does, and fixing the source beats treating symptoms.

Cleaning earns its cost when you can see dirt or mold in the runs, or after pests or building work did damage. Lacking those signs, new filters, sealed seams and controlled humidity usually do more. Cleaning without fixing the cause lets dirt return, so address the cause first.
